name: La Tène

attributes.attribute: a site in the shallows of Lake Neuchatel
source of a large hoard, found and recorded in 1858
name of the third stage of Celtic culture

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: La Tene is a place and the name of a period in Celtic art. The site sits in the shallows of Lake Neuchatel in Switzerland. Amateur explorers found a large hoard there in 1858. The mass held gold collars, iron cauldrons, silver pins, and the remains of sacrificed beasts. The site gives its name to the third stage of Celtic culture, after the Urn layer and the Hallstatt layer. The stage ran from about 500 B.C.E. to about 100 C.E. and is split into three phases.

okr.objective: Record the La Tene site and the culture stage named for it.
